diamondback_moth.about: A tiny moth with a big appetite, the diamondback moth is a global menace to crucifer crops, capable of wiping out fields if left unchecked.
effects: Feeds on leaves and creates holes, reducing photosynthesis
recommendations: Use insecticide-treated netting or Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt)
Rotate crops to disrupt lifecycle
Remove crop residues after harvest
Introduce parasitoid wasps
Use pheromone traps for monitoring

aphid.about: Small but mighty, aphids multiply fast and spread plant diseases with ease, turning lush leaves into wilted casualties.
effects: Suck sap from plant tissues leading to wilting
Excrete honeydew that attracts sooty mold
recommendations: Spray neem oil or insecticidal soap
Introduce ladybugs and lacewings
Use reflective mulches to deter aphids
Remove infested plant parts
Avoid excessive nitrogen fertilization

armyworm.about: Known as the night raiders, armyworms march in masses, stripping crops bare almost overnight.
effects: Defoliate plants rapidly in large groups
Feed on stems and fruits causing severe yield loss
Can lead to complete crop destruction
recommendations: Scout fields regularly for early detection
Use biological pesticides like Bt or Spinosad
Apply pheromone traps to disrupt mating
Encourage birds and beneficial insects
Practice crop rotation and timely planting

grasshopper.about: Jumping from plant to plant, grasshoppers can turn thriving fields into barren wastelands during dry spells.
effects: Feed on leaves, flowers, and stems
Create irregular holes in plant tissue
Cause significant defoliation in dry seasons
recommendations: Apply insecticide baits in affected zones
Keep field borders weed-free
Encourage predators like birds and spiders
Use trap crops as decoys
Apply targeted insecticides in outbreaks

whitefly.about: These tiny white invaders weaken plants and spread devastating diseases, often going unnoticed until it’s too late.
effects: Suck plant sap causing leaf curling and yellowing
Transmit viral diseases (e.g. tomato yellow leaf curl)
Excrete honeydew leading to fungal growth
recommendations: Use yellow sticky traps to monitor adults
Spray neem oil or insecticidal soap
Remove heavily infested leaves
Introduce Encarsia formosa as a biological control
Avoid susceptible crops in hot seasons
